description: EMA alpha 0.05→0.06 — checks timed out, benchmark ties
Half-hop PV (hop/2=512) with corrected consumption — regresses 945.6, near-unity and energy balance disrupted

asi.hypothesis: Match the batch hybrid's half-hop PV to double the overlap density, giving more phase modification averaging and less energy loss
asi.rollback_reason: 945.6 vs 954.1. Near-unity cases crash (percussive 1.02x freq_pres 0.89, EDM centroid 0.43) because the energy compensation, shelf, and blend parameters were all tuned for the full-hop PV. Half-hop PV has fundamentally different output characteristics.
asi.next_action_hint: Half-hop is a real architectural lever but requires retuning ALL downstream parameters (gain EMA, shelf, blend) from scratch. This is a multi-day effort, not a single-shot experiment.
asi.insight: Half-hop PV improves some mid-ratio cases (perc 1.5x batch_sim +0.02, harm 1.5x centroid +0.02) but the existing compensation stack is so tightly tuned to full-hop behavior that switching breaks everything else. A proper half-hop redesign would start from scratch on the compensation stack.

description: Streaming band-split PV (sub-bass bypass + upper PV) — catastrophic regression, sub-bass/upper alignment broken

asi.hypothesis: Split input at 200Hz, process only upper band through PV, resample sub-bass independently, then sum
asi.rollback_reason: 664.5 vs 954.1. Catastrophic regression because: (1) sub-bass resample position i/ratio doesn't match PV output position, (2) removing sub-bass from PV input changes the PV's energy/phase tracking, (3) energy compensation was trained on full-band PV output
asi.next_action_hint: Band-split streaming requires the sub-bass to also be PV-processed (not linearly resampled) to maintain temporal alignment. A dual-PV approach with proper output summing would be needed.
asi.insight: Linear resampling and PV output are temporally misaligned — the PV adds latency and modifies temporal structure, so you can't simply resample a band and add it back at the same sample positions.

description: Streaming WSOLA-PV hybrid overlay: run WSOLA on transient input, crossfade 85%→0% over PV output — 954.3 (+0.2), percussive 926.8

asi.hypothesis: On detected transient onsets at extreme ratios, run WSOLA on the same input chunk and crossfade its output over the PV output with 85% WSOLA weight for the first 30% (attack) decaying to 0% (PV takes over for decay)
asi.architecture: True streaming WSOLA-PV hybrid with per-channel WSOLA instances, pre-allocated buffers, and RT-safe crossfade
asi.breakthrough: First time the streaming path uses actual WSOLA for transient content, matching the batch hybrid concept

description: Tune WSOLA overlay: 90% weight, 25% attack window, quadratic decay — 954.5 (+0.2), percussive 927.3

asi.hypothesis: Stronger WSOLA weight (90%) with shorter attack window (25%) and smoother quadratic decay preserves more transient detail
asi.improvement: +0.2 overall, +0.5 percussive from previous, +0.4 total from pre-WSOLA baseline

description: 95% WSOLA weight, 20% attack — ties current best
